# `silk/concurrency/work_queue`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Queues that move owned values between native threads, for work-stealing schedulers.

## When to use
| Type | Use it for |
|---|---|
| [`WorkDeque`](#WorkDeque) | The work of one thread, which idle threads can steal |
| [`Injector`](#Injector) | A queue that all threads push to and take from |
| [`Mailbox`](#Mailbox) | Many threads that send to one receiver |

## Details
[`WorkDeque.make`](#WorkDeque.impl.make) returns the [`Worker`](#Worker) that owns a Chase-Lev deque. The worker pushes and
pops at the bottom with no contention. Its [`Stealer`](#Stealer)s take from the top with one
compare-exchange. The ring grows by doubling. Old rings stay allocated until the deque is
dropped, because a stealer can still read one.

[`Injector`](#Injector) is a FIFO list under a `Mutex`. [`Mailbox`](#Mailbox) is the Vyukov multi-producer,
single-consumer queue: a send is one swap and one store, with no lock.

Each pushed value moves into its own allocation (a parcel), and the queues move parcel addresses
atomically. Only the thread that wins a value reads it. Thus no thread copies a value that it
does not own.

## Errors
Each push and send allocates, so it requires `Allocator` and can fail with `OutOfMemoryError`.

## Gotchas
- [`Stealer.steal`](#Stealer.impl.steal) returns [`Steal.Retry`](#Steal.Retry) when it loses a race. The caller decides whether to
  try again.
- [`MailboxReceiver.receive`](#MailboxReceiver.impl.receive) can return `None` for a short time while a send is between its two
  steps.

## Examples
### Steal work on another thread
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.concurrency.thread_native { NativeThread, SpawnError }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.concurrency.work_queue { Steal, Stealer, WorkDeque }

// Takes the oldest value. A lost race gives Retry, so try again.
fn stealOne(stealer: Stealer<i32>) -> i32 {
  while true {
    match move stealer.steal() {
      Steal<i32>.Success { value } => {
        return value
      }
      Steal<i32>.Empty => {
        return 0
      }
      Steal<i32>.Retry => {}
    }
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn program() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError | SpawnError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut worker = run WorkDeque.make<i32>() |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  run worker.push(1) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  run worker.push(2) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let stealer = worker.stealer()
  let thief = run NativeThread.spawn(
    fn() -> i32 {
      return stealOne(move stealer)
    }
  )
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)

  // The thief takes from the top (oldest), the owner pops from the bottom (newest).
  let stolen = thief.join()
  let popped = match move worker.pop() {
    Option<i32>.Some { value } => value
    Option<i32>.None => 0
  }
  if stolen != 1 || popped != 2 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn failed<E>(error: E) -> i32 {
  drop error
  return 1
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  return run Effect.catchAll(program(), failed)
}
```

### Send through a mailbox and an injector
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.concurrency.work_queue { Injector, Mailbox }

effect fn program() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()

  // A mailbox: senders on any thread, one receiver.
  let mut receiver = run Mailbox.make<i32>() |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let sender = receiver.sender()
  run sender.send(7) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let received = match move receiver.receive() {
    Option<i32>.Some { value } => value
    Option<i32>.None => 0
  }

  // An injector: a shared FIFO queue.
  let queue = run Injector<i32>.make() |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  run queue.push(1) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  run queue.push(2) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let first = match move queue.pop() {
    Option<i32>.Some { value } => value
    Option<i32>.None => 0
  }
  if received != 7 || first != 1 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn outOfMemory(error: OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  return 1
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  return run Effect.catchAll(program(), outOfMemory)
}
```

<a id="Worker"></a>

## `Worker`

```silk
pub struct Worker<T>
```

The owner of a work-stealing deque. It pushes and pops at the bottom.

### Details
A worker is `Transferable` when `T` is, so it can move to the thread that runs the work. Push
and pop take it exclusively. [`Worker.pop`](#Worker.impl.pop) returns the newest value.

## `Injector`

```silk
pub struct Injector<T>
```

A shared FIFO queue that all threads can push to and take from.

### Details
Clones are handles to the same queue. An injector is `Transferable` and `Concurrent` when `T` is
`Transferable`. Each operation holds the lock only to link or unlink one parcel.

## `Mailbox`

```silk
pub struct Mailbox
```

The constructor of multi-producer, single-consumer mailboxes: many threads that send to one
receiver.

### Details
It is the Vyukov queue: a send is one swap and one store, with no lock. Each send allocates, so
it can fail with `OutOfMemoryError`.

### Gotchas
[`MailboxReceiver.receive`](#MailboxReceiver.impl.receive) can return `None` for a short time while a send is between its two
steps.

### Method `receive`

```silk
pub fn receive(self: &mut Self) -> Option<T>
```

Takes the oldest value sent, or reports none.

#### Gotchas

A send that has swapped itself in but not yet linked reports none until it links, so a
caller that knows a value is coming retries.
